overview:
Capvision is one of the largest expert networks headquartered in Asia and the largest expert network based in China, where it is domestically known as Kaisheng Rongying. Founded in 2006 by former Bain & Company consultants and Morgan Stanley investment bankers, the firm has built deep expertise in connecting global institutional clients with industry professionals across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. Capvision partners with over 2,000 clients including institutional investors, consulting firms, and Fortune 500 companies.

The company offers a broad suite of primary research services including expert consultations, surveys, corporate access events, customized research projects, and industry reports. With offices in Shanghai, New York, Munich, Hong Kong, Osaka, and Beijing, Capvision straddles both Asian and Western markets — a positioning that is both its key differentiator and, following the 2023 Chinese government crackdown on consulting firms, a source of ongoing regulatory complexity.

history.narrative: Capvision was founded in 2006 in Shanghai by Roger Xu and Kai Hong, both of whom came from backgrounds in management consulting and investment banking. The firm originally focused on sourcing expert advisors within China for global institutional clients, and gradually expanded its network and geographic footprint. By the early 2020s Capvision had grown to 600+ employees and was positioning for a Hong Kong IPO. However, the company's trajectory was significantly disrupted in 2023 when Chinese state security authorities raided its offices as part of a broader crackdown on consulting and due diligence firms operating in China.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Consultations
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one or group phone consultations connecting clients with industry professionals who have direct operational experience in specific sectors, companies, or markets. Capvision's strongest differentiator is sourcing experts across Greater China and the broader Asia-Pacific region.

servicesDetailed.name: Surveys
servicesDetailed.description: Quantitative and qualitative survey research leveraging Capvision's expert network to provide structured data on market conditions, competitive dynamics, and industry trends. Surveys can be paired with follow-up consultations for deeper investigation.

servicesDetailed.name: Industry Reports
servicesDetailed.description: Capvision produces and distributes industry-focused research reports drawing on its expert network and primary research capabilities, covering sectors across Asia and global markets.

servicesDetailed.name: Corporate Access / Events
servicesDetailed.description: Conferences, roundtables, and corporate access events that bring together industry experts, company management teams, and institutional investors. These events are particularly focused on Asian markets and cross-border investment themes.

servicesDetailed.name: Customized Research
servicesDetailed.description: Bespoke research projects combining expert consultations, surveys, and desk research into comprehensive deliverables tailored to specific client questions — often used for due diligence, market entry analysis, and competitive intelligence.

servicesDetailed.name: HR & Talent Services
servicesDetailed.description: Executive search and talent advisory services that leverage Capvision's expert network for recruitment and organizational consulting.

aiPlatform.narrative: Capvision has invested in technology to support expert matching and compliance workflows, though its AI capabilities are less prominently marketed compared to newer, technology-first competitors. The platform uses automated matching algorithms to connect client requests with relevant experts, and has integrated compliance automation tools to support screening and monitoring across multiple regulatory jurisdictions.
features: Automated compliance screening across Chinese and international regulatory frameworks
Natural language search for expert identification

complianceExtended.narrative: Capvision's compliance story is uniquely complex due to its position straddling Chinese and international regulatory environments. Following the May 2023 raid by Chinese state security authorities, the firm underwent a government-supervised rectification process and announced comprehensive compliance reforms. The company now operates under enhanced scrutiny in China while also maintaining compliance frameworks aligned with Western regulatory expectations around MNPI and expert vetting.
highlights: Dual compliance framework covering Chinese national security regulations and Western MNPI standards
Regional compliance teams with local regulatory knowledge in each major office
Expert screening adapted to both Chinese and international standards
Audit trail capabilities for client interactions
complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: Capvision has faced regulatory challenges on multiple fronts. In May 2023, Chinese state security authorities raided the firm's offices as part of a broader crackdown on consulting and due diligence firms, citing national security concerns about cross-border information flows. Capvision completed a government-supervised rectification and implemented new compliance protocols. The firm has also faced scrutiny from Western regulators. These experiences have made Capvision's regulatory positioning more complex than most peers, and potential clients should evaluate the firm's current compliance posture in the context of their own regulatory requirements.

clientFit.narrative: Capvision is best suited for clients who need deep Asia-Pacific expertise, particularly those with investment or business interests in China and broader Asian markets. The firm's dual-market positioning makes it especially valuable for cross-border research where understanding both Asian and Western perspectives is important.
segments: Institutional investors with Asia-Pacific portfolio exposure or investment mandates
Private equity firms conducting due diligence on Asian targets or portfolio companies
Consulting firms needing rapid access to industry experts in China, Japan, and Southeast Asia
Multinational corporations evaluating market entry or competitive dynamics in Asian markets
Research teams needing multilingual expert access across Asian languages
